observations.observation: DOI 10.1145/3711938, Article 33, February 2025, licence CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 visible in rendered page image

Authors describe an online Prolific pilot (50 participants) using six video-recorded Pepper directional utterances composited over a corn-maze video, asking preferred trust-repair responses. This is author-reported recruitment, not an admitted independent sample.

In-person physical maze with the Pepper robot recommending paths and making wrong suggestions; authors report 60 participants in six between-participant arms (two voices x three repair strategies; 10 per arm). Figure 2 visually inspected; trials and arms are not additional independent participant samples.

Both voices are synthetic. Authors compare Pepper default with custom TTS, report matched utterance duration/speech rate but materially different F0 and voice quality: mean F0 332.99 vs 225.67 Hz, mean HNR 8.61 vs 14.83 dB. Table 3 visually checked; these are author-provided stimulus descriptors, NOT independent acoustic measurement.

Authors describe investigator-controlled Wizard-of-Oz robot navigation and participant use of noise-cancelling headphones. This reading does not verify audio files, stimulus authenticity, or acoustics independently.
